perspectives.title: Debt Impact

representative_posts.author: beijingpalmer.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I don’t think this is true! Debt is much more destabilizing and painful.

representative_posts.author: lawyerforcat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I don't understand why people keep saying this wasn't a debt. If someone sent me $500k bills for 3 years I would sure believe it was a debt.

representative_posts.author: shiftercat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: And before anyone jumps in saying that getting into debt is just evidence of poor choices... sometimes emergencies happen that require a loan or credit card. Then imagine someone losing their job shortly after. You don't necessarily know someone's circumstances.

representative_posts.author: ajaxsinger.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Final thought: the people I've met who are most rational about both debt and windfalls have tended to be the people who live closest to the edge financially. Most of them have had both and neither has done much to create a permanent change in circumstance.

representative_posts.author: raptornx01.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: they're all in huge debt, its just that part of that debt was paying off the right people to make sure they could hold off on paying that debt.

representative_posts.author: ltremmick.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Also, sounds like a fair amount of time and effort went in to getting that debt written off.

representative_posts.author: arthurwyatt.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Okay so it’s “net worth” so all the debt means there would be way less of them.

representative_posts.author: thetecheng.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Do they? I've been on the recieving end of windfalls and unexpected debts of roughly this magnitude, and while the debt was annoying and deferred some other purchases I dont think it meaningfully altered my life.

representative_posts.author: shnyblkfbishoes.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It seems like they started out playing a shell game with the debt, using many shells to hide it, but over time those shells have been reduced, leaving the debt under the last one. Once that final shell is lifted, the debt is revealed, and we face a default.

representative_posts.author: nateobermiller.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yeah, because debt collectors certainly look at lifetime earnings when they're trying to figure out how to get their money back

representative_posts.author: legndofphoenix.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: There's a big difference between working when you don't have debt vs throwing your money into a debt hole for years.

representative_posts.author: thetecheng.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You most debt collectors will try to get you on some sort of income based repayment plan, which is basically lifetime earnings with the added benefit of accounting for the fact that you may not be in your prime earning years.

representative_posts.author: cuw.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: hey the discussion was actually about a massive amount of debt being rectified from $500k to $30k and if you don't think $470k in debt remediation has a large net effect you are dumb as dirt

representative_posts.author: artist12.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If that's true then pay down the debt and send us all a huge rebate! I won't hold my breath!

representative_posts.author: t0wnp1ann3r.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: He says they have studies of what happens when people do get those windfalls... But what are the odds the windfalls are distributed like the wealth, mostly to people who weren't in the red in the first place? There's a dichotomy between people who have assets and people who have debt.

representative_posts.author: cdg.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I have never heard this ever before! Do economists assume a general audience understands this distinction? not being cheeky I’m actually wondering 😭 and also like. what if someone was gonna kill themselves and then didn’t bc they’re no longer in crazy debt? is stuff like that asked abt in studies?

representative_posts.author: rivertam.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think this stuff is sufficiently complicated to the point that most people don't understand it but the key is that if I send you an invoice for a million dollars you aren't a million dollars in debt until I admit it was a mistake.

representative_posts.author: lawyerforcat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If a hospital tells you that you have a $500k debt for 3 years, and that hospital has the power to send you to collections, sue you, and garnish your wages, how is that not a debt? A debt that is later lowered or determined to be invalid is still a debt. Also the OP posted more details elsewhere:

representative_posts.author: doomandgloom1951.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Here is a solution. Cancel all debts owed by poor nations.

representative_posts.author: rhiolit.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: consumer debt is a significant source of financial stress and stress has a lot of documented negative health effects, as well as knock-on effects on your relationships if you’re struggling to manage it

representative_posts.author: foxglove.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You will never owe them anything, because it's not something that could even qualify as debt. They can't bring your dead friends back, they can't fix the relationships that failed under the strain, they can't compensate for the lost time, even if they were inclined to, which they aren't.

Business.name: Thirty Thousand

perspectives.title: 30k Life Changing
perspectives.summary: 30k is a life-changing amount of money

representative_posts.author: tanosski.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Tell me you're out of touch by saying 30k isn't a life changing amount of money lmaoo.

representative_posts.author: alexisjanson.com
representative_posts.text: Sounds like there’s some discourse whether 30k is life-changing to avg person I will posit it IS, because large lump sums of money get spent differently than paychecks. Some of these “impulse buys” are big boosts if applied right, others could haunt you (a house you can’t afford) Life-changing!

representative_posts.author: turnitup5000db.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 30k is a downpayment on a house, which is a life-changing event. Could also fix a mountain of credit card debt, or replace a car. All three of those could be life changing in the right circumstances. Just depends on your situation.

representative_posts.author: realabby.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The amount of privilege you have to have to say $30k isn’t life changing is unreal. Even at my most well off I would have considered $10k life changing just because that bump of free money would have let me pay off debt or get ahead and live more comfortably for a time, which has a snowball effect.

representative_posts.author: jamesqpurcell.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 30k would leave me debt free and able to invest more time into my hobbies that could be personally profitable. I think you don’t appreciate the value of $1000, let alone 30 of them. To someone who makes less then 50 or 60k a year. Taking the pressure off for a year is life changing for most people.

representative_posts.author: geg3npressing.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This somewhat exposes the disconnect here. I think Matt is (rightly) saying that $30k could—or perhaps *should*—be a life-changing amount of money. I don’t think economists are disputing that. The economists are saying that it *hasn’t* been life-changing for most who have gotten $30k windfalls.

representative_posts.author: mindyoursnotmine.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: $30K would be life changing for me and my kids. Shoot $500 would be month changing.

representative_posts.author: redoubters.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: "$30k is not 'life-changing' money for the vast majority of people" is in no way arguing that it would not improve people's lives, maybe significantly. It is also not arguing that we should be cutting benefits or anything like that you have imagined an argument and gotten mad at it for some reason

representative_posts.author: iloveoutside.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think 30k dollars is a life or death amount of money. if I was on the bridge, about to jump off, and someone gave me 30k dollars, I wouldn't jump. that's by definition life changing.

representative_posts.author: 8bitblunder.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Hrm or maybe you have a lot of people who know people for whom $30k would be life changing but because you and Matt have never met nor been poor or desperate in your lives, the life-changing effects of $30k to most people look like things you take for granted. Maybe we were those people, once.

representative_posts.author: nicebart.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 30K is 85% of the highest annual amount I’ve ever been paid in my life. I’m thirty fucking years old. who are these silver spoon fucking morons

representative_posts.author: beasmeeply.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If $30k today all at once wouldn't change your life you had better be rounding up for charity at the checkout every time my boy

representative_posts.author: saluk64007.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Why are you arguing about *receiving* 30k. The family had to pay it. On top of their regular bills, their monthly healthcare costs, and increased expenses of parenthood. I guarantee they had extra financial hardships throughout, which changed their life in the short term of the 3 years.

representative_posts.author: shaneanderson.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: So If someone stole $30k from you, it wouldn't affect your life? 30k is the difference between having a car and not. That's over a year of mortgage payments. The stress relief alone would LITERALLY improve your helath and life span. *Literally*: life changing.

representative_posts.author: allanshoe.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think the sentiment is to compare what $30k is all at once (falling off a building which will be fatal) and how that you will make $2m over your life (walk up thousands of steps over the course of your life) and how Matt's conclusion and rationalization is absurd.

representative_posts.author: forevernowhere.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Losing or gaining $30k in one go could be life-changing for some. Recently my uncle sold his company and gave every long-term employee £10k on top of redundancy pay. It didn’t seem huge to us, but some were in tears. One person actually said, ‘This is life-changing.’ It’s all about perspective.

You end up thinking "this wasn't a problem for me; these people must be morons or liars"

representative_posts.author: davallone.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This year I had a life-changing financial payday that was well short of $100K AND a $200K-ish medical bill that my (very good/union provided) insurance knocked down to $900. So a lot of that argument was relevant to my recent experiences…

representative_posts.author: smoke1966.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: all insurance does is protect the wealthy corporations from massive losses..

representative_posts.author: isomorphism.net
representative_posts.text: Insurance defends itself with "we get deals for the consumer, we can bargain in aggregate". This is something a financial intermediary does. If we want to maintain a private insurance model we should make them our aggregate financial intermediary. This means nobody gets bills from the hospital.

representative_posts.author: ottersimple.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Requiring insurance is taking their weapons away. That's what you do when people don't pay their insurance.

representative_posts.author: flat5flat9.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: We all know that insurance companies do all they can to deny claims, but takes it to the level of corruption and malignancy.

representative_posts.author: isomorphism.net
representative_posts.text: The thing about insurance, as a whole model, is that you can amortize risk across a population or across time, but the model that works out cheapest for everybody all the time is one that is amortized across both, and in order to do that you can't opt out when it's cheap.

representative_posts.author: infinitehydra.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Oh. I just saw your Wikipedia page. You're an MBA, not an economist. I understand now why you were so confused about how insurance works.

representative_posts.author: grandmotherboy.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: also refrain from telling your life insurance company you drive a jumping deathbox or that premium will skyrocket as well. ☠️

representative_posts.author: sunnydarkgreen.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: When media, govt and business are only paying lip service at best, its hard to see what insurance industry can do, beyond the price signals and coverage triage (for which politicians often attack insurers).

representative_posts.author: skiskinnyskis.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: And it's clear why the health insurance industry engages in such practices like double billing and overbilling- as there are a certain percentage of people who don't fight but rather just pay out of fear, panic, or simply not wanting to deal with the purposely burdensome administrative hurdles.

representative_posts.author: brunocatarino.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: That's how car insurance works, isn't it? If you never had an accident, you don't need insurance, everybody knows that... 😒

representative_posts.author: nolehongo.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: begging for insurance

representative_posts.author: eyegah.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It will be a system-wide triage. Emergencies first. If you have a health issue you will wait for care unless it becomes an emergency. But even with that, it makes more sense than what we have now. Even people with “really good” insurance still pay OOP.

representative_posts.author: corgirules2.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: dealing with this vary issue. Suddenly the place I've lived for over 20 yrs has become a fire risk, yet no one can show me how this has been substantiated. It's a pass the buck situation, insurance Co blames underwriters, underwriters blame pressure from insurance companies...it's been a nightmare

representative_posts.author: shadefawks.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I remember when car insurance went down every year as you and your car got older...

representative_posts.author: 2puru2partisan.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If your car got wrecked and you spent three years under the assumption the insurance company was making you pay the entire cost of repair out of pocket until they went oops your recollection of those events would not start with how much money you saved with Geico correct

representative_posts.author: boudiccamic.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It will be interesting to see how much my insurance premium goes up. Last 2 years, my net widow’s pension went down after the COLA because the insurance premium increase was larger than the COLA.

representative_posts.author: isomorphism.net
representative_posts.text: You cannot make a private insurance model work within a reasonable delta of an amount people pay if there's no mandate to buy insurance. Like, if they dropped tax incentives for employee provided insurance right now today half of America under 30 would drop it voluntarily which would be terrible.

representative_posts.author: flyingcorgi.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My insurance advisor wisely counseled me against the Advantage plans when it was my time to sign up, and I am forever grateful for his advice. I hope I am never forced into one.

representative_posts.author: carriagereturn.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yup, I saw the fall out of the discourse while I was on the phone with my insurance company (...ha) and only just put two and two together of where this all started which ... Damn.

representative_posts.text: I don’t even know why people over 65 want private insurance.. if you look at the things they cover there is nothing that benefits older people.. in fact private HC is just another govt rort brought to you by John Howard and his rich mates

representative_posts.author: monsterteatime.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Getting insurance companies to eventually settle on less than they were going to gauge you for is 1. not a "paperwork error" 2. stressful af during which you are either post medical or still dealing with a medical crisis 3. in no way about the actual cost of anything.

representative_posts.author: jfs.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It's also WONDERFUL for self-employment and entrepreneurs because insurance is always available. You don't need to have an employer to survive. The risk-shifting setup seemed better than the ACA, but I forget why I thought so.

representative_posts.author: shadefawks.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I switched off Progressive because my insurance went from $700 every 6 months to $1300 in less than 2 years. I've had no claims or tickets for years. My current insurance was much cheaper but is still going up like $100 every 6 months

representative_posts.author: stevewarren209.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 3/ "Private" insurance is a for-profit enterprise which covers SOME people for SOME things (or maybe not) & splits the difference between what you pay in premiums & what they pay out as dividends to billionaire shareholders and $20 million salaries to execs who decide whether or not you're covered.

representative_posts.author: realmmccoy.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Is it bad to spend $ like you're nearly dead and insurance will take care of it? I am getting more free spending as I decay feels like.

representative_posts.author: ukpolitics.papernaut.co
representative_posts.text: THE INDEPENDENT: From 6 November, UK law will ban porn depicting strangulation, incest and adults pretending to be under 16, following cross-party pressure over its impact on women and girls. - by Harry Taylor

representative_posts.author: lamuradex.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: capnshores.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Thats non-consent. And thus, assault. The idea that porn is somehow ‘corrupting’ people into doing awful things, rather than it being a healthy outlet or even a vibrant subculture and economic factor of society, is absurd.

representative_posts.author: chorizo-chomper.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: lordmimey.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The porn ban isn't about morality, but about justifying a police state. Everything else from that is simply smoke and mirrors. representative_posts.author: magscampbell.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I did not like that BBC headline the other day about choking and incest being banned in porn. Conflating kink and incest, making them sound equally disgusting, is so wrong. I find the lack of details as alarming as the INSANE overreach. like holy shit this is a slippery slope... Idc if these are your kinks or not, banning certain kinks protects no one and harms EVERYONE.

perspectives.summary: Porn has various effects on people

representative_posts.author: nicoletenshi.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You don't solve that by making sure no one could ever possibly see that kind of porn, you solve it by giving people, ESPECIALLY young people, information that corrects the passive misinfo they get from the culture

representative_posts.author: erikahall.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The problem is porn fills the gap left by a lack of sex education, which should include relationships, consent, communication, power dynamics, cultural scripts, and how to recognize and exit unsafe situations. I am angrier at a lot of romcoms than I am at porn.

representative_posts.author: nicoletenshi.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This is what gets me, there are like ACTUAL problems with how a lot of what is presented front and center as the Most Normal Standard Material if you go looking for porn is stuff that features dangerous violence without any form of disclaimer but that's not a porn problem it's an info problem

representative_posts.author: erikahall.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Apart from CSAM and non-consensual porn, and probably something else evil I'm forgetting, I take a pretty hard line on not criminalizing porn because it's a wide net that catches all sorts of expression and doesn't achieve its purported goals.

representative_posts.author: squidfromspace.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Which is the whole ball game (if you'll forgive the pun), and always has been. I don't think there can be much argument that a lot of porn is misogynistic, and that that's a problem. But this is a symptom of the *actual* disease, which is a failure to treat women's autonomy seriously in society.

representative_posts.author: secretman11.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You've got your causality backwards People don't have violent fantasies because they saw violent porn.
